title: Dynamic credit rebalancer tuning and graceful-degradation for small-tenant burst shortfalls
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Customers (notably SparkHealth and a mid-market fintech pilot) reported recurrent degraded throughput and silent coldstarts during burst windows despite appearing to have available burst credits in the reserved pool ledger. This ticket drives a combined short-term mitigation and a long-term redesign of the credit rebalancer heuristic to avoid credit fragmentation and to provide graceful degradation for small tenants.

Observed behavior / impact:
- Symptom: multiple small tenants (low steady-state qps, high burstiness) observed token-level latency spikes and 429s during simulated traffic waves. Dashboard spike correlated with reserved-pool depletion alerts for the region, but per-tenant burst-credit ledger showed nonzero balances.
- Customer-visible effects: transient request failures, elevated tail latency for chat/generate endpoints, and at least two enterprise support escalations over a 48-hour window.
- Frequency: intermittent — appears when leader re-election/reassignment coincides with simultaneous burst windows across many small-tenancy namespaces.

Investigation notes (timeline):
- 2026-02-24: First support escalation from SparkHealth. Eng on-call reproduced issue in staging with synthetic workload.
- 2026-02-25: Initial hotfix (v1) deployed to limit credit reclamation rate; reduced customer-facing 429s by about 40%. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- 2026-02-26 — 2026-03-02: Deep dive into allocator/rebalancer logs. Found three contributing factors: leader reassignment double-counting, micro-fragmentation of burst-credit shards, and over-aggressive immediate reclamation after tenant detach.
- 2026-03-04: Telemetry added for per-tenant ledger deltas and rebalancer decisions (dashboard: https://analytics.redwood.ai/dashboards/credit-rebalancer-ops).
- 2026-03-07: Repro harness validated race: leader flip while rebalancer is mid-pass leaves credits in limbo and owner pointers inconsistent for ~30s window — enough to trigger coldstarts at peak.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by logs):
1) The rebalancer assumes atomic transfer of shard ownership during leader reassignment; the two-phase window allows both old and new leader to mark credits as reclaimed leading to logical duplication or temporary orphaning.
2) The burst-credit allocator aggressively reclaims fractional credit shards from small-tenant buckets whenever global headroom drops, but does not account for in-flight KV cache warmups, causing self-inflicted coldstarts.

Short-term mitigations already applied (v1):
- Reclaim-rate throttling: cap rebalancer work per-second per-leader to reduce double-work windows. Deployed 2026-02-25 (PR #4821).
- Conservative hold: when leader transition detected, broker retains a conservative hold of 1s before finalizing shard ownership to allow in-flight updates to settle.
- Customer fallbacks: configured SparkHealth to route to a higher-tier fallback model for 60s during detected rebalances.
Effect: 40% reduction in reported incidents; still not acceptable for P0 SLA customers.

Planned long-term solution (v2):
- Credit-transfer protocol: implement idempotent transfer tokens for shard moves so both leaders can safely reconcile without double-counting. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Credit+Transfer+Protocol
- Fragment consolidation: periodic compaction job that runs off the hot path to merge fractional shards back into tenant-level buckets (configurable frequency).
- Graceful degradation policy: introduce 'soft-headroom' per-tenant that allows limited temporary over-provisioning during KV warmups; paired with a token-bucket honest accounting to avoid cross-tenant starvation.
- Canary plan: rollout to a single noncritical region (eu-west-2) with telemetry gates (error-rate < 0.5% and tail-latency not increased).

Implementation breakdown (milestones):
- M1 (this sprint): design review, proto PR for idempotent transfer token and throttling knobs. Owner: Miguel. Estimate: 3 pts. Target: 2026-03-08 (design complete).
- M2: implement token protocol + unit tests + e2e harness; add compaction job. Owner: Systems team. Estimate: 5 pts. Target: 2026-03-21.
- M3: canary deployment and rollback plan; monitor dashboards and customer health. Owner: SRE. Estimate: 3 pts. Target: 2026-03-28.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency vs availability: fully serializing shard transfers eliminates the race but increases leader transfer latency during upgrades. We prefer idempotent eventual reconciliation to keep failover fast.
- Immediate compaction on hot path reduces fragmentation quickly but risks adding CPU pressure; chosen approach is periodic off-peak compaction.

Open questions / risks:
- How many legacy tenant shards will need backfill reconciling after protocol switch? (Mitigation: migration utility to sweep and fix historical orphan shards.)
- Can compaction cause bursty CPU/IO on overloaded nodes? (Mitigation: adaptive backoff and concurrency limits.)

Review feedback and approvals:
- PM review: Lina Zhao approved approach and asked to include SLAs for fallback promotion times.
- Design review: Notes attached in Confluence page; security review waived for v2 since no new customer data is introduced.

Action items (next 7 days):
- [x] Deploy v1 reclaim-rate throttle (done 2026-02-25).
- [x] Add telemetry for ledger deltas (done 2026-03-04).
- [ ] Submit design PR for idempotent transfer tokens (owner: Miguel) — in progress (branch: feature/credit-token).
- [ ] Implement compaction job proto and safety knobs (owner: Systems).
- [ ] Prepare canary plan and notify support/SEs; create runbook for manual rollback.

Links / artifacts:

- Design doc (credit transfer protocol): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Credit+Transfer+Protocol
- Postmortem draft (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Burst+Credit+Fragmentation+Postmortem

Notes for support and customer comms:
- Support should communicate that we deployed an interim mitigation that reduced incidents; a full fix is scheduled for rollout over the next two sprints with a canary-first approach.
- Offer affected customers an ops pairing session during canary to validate behavior against their workload.

History of updates:
- 2026-03-01: Added telemetry and reproduced race locally.
- 2026-03-07: Confirmed double-counting bug; drafted protocol.
- 2026-03-14: Design PR posted; moved ticket to In Progress.

If you are triaging: prioritize the design PR review and the canary runbook. Miguel to post PR link when ready and tag SRE for rollout windows.
